sentences.en: An old woman, who was known by the subriquet of Mother Crackham, rather startled me by rushing up as I stood at the fireplace and demanded to know if I was Jack the Ripper.
sentences.zh: 一位被称为“克拉克汉姆妈妈”的老妇人，在我站在壁炉旁时冲过来，问我是不是“开膛手杰克”，这让我相当吃惊。

sentences.en: The awkwardness of answering this question I was happily relieved of by the old dame herself assuring me that she did not think I was.
sentences.zh: 这位老太太自己向我保证她并不认为我是那个人，这让我从回答这个尴尬问题的困境中解脱了出来。

sentences.en: I know you ain't him, she said.
sentences.zh: 她说，我知道你不是他。

sentences.en: You wouldn't rip me up, would you now?
sentences.zh: 你不会把我剖开，对吧？

sentences.en: By and by, the proceedings in the kitchen became more lively.
sentences.zh: 不久之后，厨房里的气氛变得活跃起来。

sentences.en: Girls commenced singing songs and the poet of the company entertained the room with the chorus of his latest composition.
sentences.zh: 姑娘们开始唱歌，席间的诗人还用他最新创作的合唱曲招待大家。

sentences.en: Has anyone seen him?
sentences.zh: 有人见过他吗？

sentences.en: Can you tell us where he is?
sentences.zh: 你能告诉我们他在哪儿吗？

sentences.en: If you meet him, you must take away his knife.
sentences.zh: 如果你遇见他，一定要夺走他的刀。

sentences.en: Then give him to the women.
sentences.zh: 然后把他交给女人们。

sentences.en: That'll spoil his pretty fizz.
sentences.zh: 那会毁了他那张漂亮的脸蛋。

sentences.en: And I wouldn't give him tuppence for his life.
sentences.zh: 我可不会花两便士买他的命。

sentences.en: Now at night when you're undressed and about to go to rest, just see that he ain't underneath the bed.
sentences.zh: 现在，当你在晚上脱衣准备休息时，一定要看看他是不是躲在床底下。

sentences.en: If he is, you mustn't shout, but politely drag him out.
sentences.zh: 如果他在那儿，你千万别大喊大叫，要礼貌地把他拖出来。

sentences.en: And with your poker, tap him on the head.
sentences.zh: 然后用你的火钳敲他的头。

sentences.en: So that, Dominic, was the evening news published on the 5th of October, 1888,
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，以上就是 1888 年 10 月 5 日发布的晚间新闻，

sentences.en: by a top investigative journalist describing the atmosphere in Cooney's lodging house on the notorious Flower and Dean Street,
sentences.zh: 由一位顶级调查记者描述了臭名昭著的弗劳尔迪恩街上库尼旅馆里的气氛，

sentences.zh: 那家旅馆正是“开膛手杰克”最新受害者曾住过的地方。

sentences.en: And we are, of course, in Spitalfields, in Whitechapel, in the east end of London.
sentences.zh: 我们现在当然是在伦敦东区的白教堂，斯皮塔佛德。

sentences.en: It's the autumn of 1888.
sentences.zh: 那是 1888 年的秋天。

sentences.en: And we are deep into the story of the most notorious murderer of all time, Jack the Ripper.
sentences.zh: 我们正在深入探讨史上最臭名昭著的杀手——“开膛手杰克”的故事。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And the lodging house, judging by that reading, full of Australians, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，从那段阅读来看，那家旅馆里住满了澳大利亚人。

sentences.en: It wasn't Australians.
sentences.zh: 那不是澳大利亚人。

sentences.en: It was Cockneys.
sentences.zh: 那是伦敦土著。

sentences.zh: 可爱的伦敦土著。

sentences.en: That sounds like Russell Crowe to me.
sentences.zh: 听起来像是罗素·克劳。

sentences.zh: 嗯，澳大利亚口音确实源自伦敦土著口音。

sentences.zh: 当然是这样。

sentences.en: Couldn't be more Cockney.
sentences.zh: 再没有比这更像伦敦土著的了。

sentences.en: And it's a kind of, it's a reminder of just how obsessed by this point everybody is with the story of Jack the Ripper.
sentences.zh: 这提醒了我们，当时每个人对“开膛手杰克”的故事是多么痴迷。

sentences.en: Not just in London, not just across Britain, but across the whole world.
sentences.zh: 不仅是在伦敦，不仅是在英国，而是全世界。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: And I guess the reason for that is that no one knows who he is.
sentences.zh: 我想原因在于没人知道他是谁。

sentences.en: And that, of course, remains the case to this day.
sentences.zh: 当然，这一点至今仍然如此。

sentences.en: So why are people so fascinated?
sentences.zh: 那么为什么人们如此着迷呢？

sentences.en: Partly because the case seems to embody some of the anxieties of late Victorian London, but also the inherent fascination of the case.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是这个案件似乎体现了维多利亚时代晚期伦敦的一些焦虑，但也因为案件本身固有的吸引力。

sentences.en: It's so savage and so horrific, but also that mystery, right?
sentences.zh: 它太残忍、太恐怖了，但同时也充满了神秘感，对吧？

sentences.en: That he's the thief in the night, the ghost in the shadows who's escaping.
sentences.zh: 他就像黑夜里的窃贼，阴影中的幽灵，正在逃之夭夭。

sentences.en: And that's, of course, why we're still so fascinated and why, almost uniquely among serial killer stories, this one has an extraordinary hold on the world's imagination.
sentences.zh: 当然，这就是为什么我们至今仍如此着迷，也是为什么在连环杀手的故事中，这一个在世界想象力中占据了非同寻常的地位。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I think also what we shouldn't overlook is the sheer terror that he is inspiring.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为我们不应忽视他所激发的纯粹恐惧。

sentences.en: Because those songs, you know, you sing them to keep your spirits up, but they're expressive of an absolute dread.
sentences.zh: 因为那些歌，你知道，你唱它们是为了振奋精神，但它们表达的是一种绝对的恐惧。

sentences.en: People are terrified.
sentences.zh: 人们非常害怕。

sentences.en: Of course, and with good reason.
sentences.zh: 当然，而且理由充分。

sentences.en: So we entered last time on a cliffhanger.
sentences.zh: 上次我们是在悬念中结束的。

sentences.en: So let's remind ourselves where we've got to.
sentences.zh: 让我们回顾一下我们讲到了哪里。

sentences.en: I mean, the reason people are terrified is that there have been a series of horrific crimes.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，人们感到恐惧的原因是发生了一系列可怕的罪行。

sentences.en: The death, first of all, of Martha Tabram on the 7th of August, then Marianne or Polly Nichols on the 31st of August, her body literally ripped apart, ripped open.
sentences.zh: 首先是 8 月 7 日玛莎·塔布拉姆的死亡，然后是 8 月 31 日玛丽安或波莉·尼科尔斯的死亡，她的尸体被彻底撕裂、剖开。

sentences.en: And then another body ripped open, that of Annie Chapman on the 8th of September in a backyard at Hanbury Street, Spittlefields.
sentences.zh: 接着是 9 月 8 日在斯皮塔佛德汉伯里街的一个后院里，另一具尸体——安妮·查普曼的尸体被剖开。

sentences.en: And we entered last time on the night of Saturday the 29th and Sunday the 30th of September, when the killer has struck again, not once, but twice.
sentences.zh: 上次我们讲到了 9 月 29 日星期六到 9 月 30 日星期日那个晚上，凶手再次作案，而且不是一次，是两次。

sentences.en: So first of all, we had the discovery of the body of Elizabeth Stride, just inside Dutfields Yard, which is just outside a socialist club for Russian and Polish Jewish immigrants.
sentences.zh: 首先，我们在达特菲尔德院内发现了伊丽莎白·斯泰德的尸体，那里就在一家为俄罗斯和波兰犹太移民开设的社会主义俱乐部外面。

sentences.en: And then 45 minutes later, as we described last time, P.C.
sentences.zh: 然后 45 分钟后，正如我们上次描述的那样，警员

sentences.zh: 爱德华·沃特金斯正在奥尔盖特附近的米特广场巡逻。

sentences.en: So that's just inside the boundary of the city of London, so to the west of the other crimes.
sentences.zh: 那刚好在伦敦市的边界内，所以是在其他犯罪地点的西边。

sentences.en: And he flashes his lantern, he finds something huddled on the ground, and then he's rushing across the square where we ended last time.
sentences.zh: 他闪动灯笼，发现地上蜷缩着什么东西，然后他冲过广场，也就是我们上次结束的地方。

sentences.en: So a watchman, for God's sake, mate, come to my assistance, there's another woman cut to pieces.
sentences.zh: 所以，守夜人，看在上帝的份上，伙计，快来帮我，又有一个女人被切成碎片了。

sentences.en: So let's pick up the story.
sentences.zh: 让我们继续讲这个故事。

sentences.zh: 大约一刻钟内，一群警察聚集在尸体周围，大约 2 点 20 分，城市警察外科医生弗雷德里克·戈登·布朗医生也赶到了。

sentences.en: And it's from him that we get the, again, gruesome details of the crime scene.
sentences.zh: 正是从他那里，我们得到了犯罪现场那些令人毛骨悚然的细节。

sentences.en: So to reiterate, if you are driving along with very small children in the back, listening to a podcast about the Jack the Ripper,
sentences.zh: 所以重申一下，如果你正开车带着很小的孩子在后座，听着关于“开膛手杰克”的播客，

sentences.en: you will be unsurprised to hear that there are some gruesome details to come.
sentences.zh: 听到接下来会有一些令人毛骨悚然的细节，你一定不会感到惊讶。

sentences.en: So rethink your choices.
sentences.zh: 所以重新考虑一下你的选择吧。

sentences.zh: 弗雷德里克·戈登·布朗医生说，受害者仰面躺着，喉咙被割开，尸体被残忍地毁坏了。

sentences.en: Quote him,
sentences.zh: 引用他的话，

sentences.en: So this is a really unsettling, you know, unbelievably unsettling and strange scene, almost kind of ritualistic.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常令人不安的，你知道，令人难以置信地不安和奇怪的场景，几乎带有一种仪式感。

sentences.en: You know, what kind of killer places the victim's innards around the body?
sentences.zh: 你知道，什么样的杀手会把受害者的内脏摆在尸体周围？

sentences.en: Maybe I'm a sonic one.
sentences.zh: 也许我是个声波杀手。

sentences.zh: 好吧，也许我们应该在第五集里讲到这个。

sentences.zh: 当然，开膛手再次极其高效且迅速地作案，然后消失在夜色中。

sentences.en: So to quote Philip Sugden, whose book on the Jack the Ripper case is the definitive history.
sentences.zh: 引用菲利普·萨格登的话，他关于“开膛手杰克”案件的书是权威历史。

sentences.en: He says, you know, this probably took less than 15 minutes.
sentences.zh: 他说，你知道，这可能用了不到 15 分钟。

sentences.en: In that period of time, the killer must have got his victim into Mitre Square, assuming she's not there already, killed her.
sentences.zh: 在那段时间里，凶手一定已经把受害者带到了米特广场（假设她还没在那儿），杀死了她。

sentences.en: Mutilated her, done all his sort of operations on the body, and then got away.
sentences.zh: 毁坏了她的尸体，对尸体进行了他那种手术，然后逃之夭夭。

sentences.en: And he has taken with him her womb and her left kidney.
sentences.zh: 他带走了她的子宫和左肾。

sentences.en: And once again, he has done this almost completely unseen and undetected.
sentences.zh: 而且再一次，他几乎完全没有被看见、没有被发现。

sentences.en: So we're still in the small hours of Sunday, the 30th of September, and we now have two murder investigations going on simultaneously.
sentences.zh: 所以我们现在还在 9 月 30 日星期日的凌晨，我们现在同时有两起谋杀案在调查中。

sentences.en: So there's the Elizabeth Stride one in Whitechapel, and there's this other one now in the City of London.
sentences.zh: 一个是白教堂的伊丽莎白·斯泰德案，另一个是现在伦敦市的这起案件。

sentences.zh: 如果你想加入他们，只需前往 therestishistory.com。

sentences.en: So she had been seen in a cheap lodging house in Florendine Street just before 7 o'clock.
sentences.zh: 她在 7 点之前曾在弗洛伦丁街的一家廉价旅馆被看到过。

sentences.en: We don't know when she went out exactly.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道她具体是什么时候出去的。

sentences.en: We don't know where she was going.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道她要去哪里。

sentences.en: We don't know whether she was going out to try to solicit to get money for a bed.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道她出去是不是为了拉客赚取住宿费。

sentences.en: All of this is very unclear.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都非常不清楚。

sentences.en: We know that at some time that evening, she ate some bread and cheese, and she possibly had some drinks.
sentences.zh: 我们知道那天晚上某个时候，她吃了一些面包和奶酪，可能还喝了一些酒。

sentences.en: And she also got hold of some hard sweets, kind of breath fresheners.
sentences.zh: 她还弄到了一些硬糖，类似于清新口气的东西。

sentences.en: I think they're called cashew or something, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 我想它们叫腰果糖还是什么的，对吧？

sentences.zh: 她手里正拿着它们。

sentences.zh: 她还拿了一朵红玫瑰，别在胸前。

sentences.zh: 是的，我去调查了所有发生过这些事的地方。

sentences.zh: 而不是说你不会躺下，你肯定不会选择躺在泥地里，对吧。

sentences.zh: 为什么没有任何挣扎的迹象？

sentences.en: On the other hand, a lot of Ripper sort of scholars say, you know, the modus operandi is similar.

sentences.en: A victim killed while lying on the ground in a dark corner of the east end, the throat cut from left to right.
sentences.zh: 受害者是在东区一个黑暗角落里躺着时被杀的，喉咙从左到右被割开。

sentences.en: So the balance of probability, I think, is that this was a Jack the Ripper crime.

sentences.en: And in that case, the explanation for why the body isn't mutilated is that actually when that guy and his cart that we talked about last time, Louis Diemschutz, came into the yard,
sentences.zh: 如果是这样的话，为什么尸体没有被毁坏的解释就是，当那个我们上次谈到的带着马车的家伙，路易斯·迪姆舒茨，进入院子时，

sentences.zh: 大约12点45分，他路过达特菲尔德院子时，正如斯旺森总督察在笔记中所述，他看到一个男人停下来与一个站在门口的女人说话。

sentences.zh: 利普斯基在东区是一个非常响亮的名字，因为在1887年，一个做雨伞的家伙叫伊斯雷尔·利普斯基，他原本是另一个波兰犹太人，

sentences.zh: 我同意，福尔摩斯。

sentences.en: I agree, Holmes.
sentences.zh: 我只是想让你保持警惕。

sentences.en: I'm just trying to keep you on your toes.
sentences.zh: 好的，非常好。

sentences.en: Okay, very good.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 好了，这就是当晚的第一起罪行。

sentences.en: All right, so that's the first crime of the night.
sentences.zh: 那是伊丽莎白·斯泰德谋杀案。

sentences.en: That's Elizabeth Stride murder.
sentences.zh: 现在我们来谈第二起罪行。

sentences.en: Let's do the second crime now.
sentences.zh: 这就是在城里米特广场发现的被极其残忍地毁坏的尸体。

sentences.en: So this is the hideously mutilated body found in Mitre Square in the city.
sentences.zh: 起初，警方发现很难确认她的身份。

sentences.en: At first, the police found it very hard to identify her.
sentences.zh: 她显然是一个非常贫穷的女人。

sentences.en: She's clearly a very poor woman.
sentences.zh: 她穿着非常破旧肮脏的衣服。

sentences.en: She's wearing very old and dirty clothes.
sentences.zh: 她有两个粘土烟斗和一块手帕，还有两张当铺票，但都是假名。

sentences.en: She's got a couple of clay pipes and a handkerchief, and she's got two pawnbroker's tickets, but they're under false names.
sentences.zh: 这对于那些处于社会底层的人来说很常见。

sentences.en: That's very common for people who are kind of on the underclass, as it were.
sentences.zh: 最终，她的伴侣站了出来，一个叫约翰·凯利的劳工。

sentences.en: And eventually, her partner comes forward, a labourer called John Kelly.
sentences.zh: 他一直和她住在这个廉价公寓里，

sentences.en: He has been living with her in this DOS house,
sentences.zh: 库尼寄宿处，那是一个非常破旧的地方。

sentences.en: Cooney's lodgings house, which is a really run-down place.
sentences.zh: 他说，这是我的伴侣。

sentences.en: And he says, this is my partner.
sentences.zh: 这基本上是我的女朋友，凯特·康威。

sentences.en: This is basically my girlfriend, Kate Conway.
sentences.zh: 其实，她不叫凯特·康威。

sentences.en: Actually, her name is not Kate Conway.
sentences.zh: 她是凯瑟琳·埃多斯，今年46岁。

sentences.en: She's Catherine Eddowes, and she was 46 years old.
sentences.zh: 菲利普·塞尔克顿形容她是所有受害者中最讨人喜欢的，这并不奇怪，汤姆，因为她来自伍尔弗汉普顿。

sentences.en: Philip Selkton describes her as the most likable of all the victims, which is not surprising, Tom, because she's from Wolverhampton.
sentences.zh: 所以我给你简单勾勒一下凯瑟琳·埃多斯的生活，因为，同样，因为我们想让受害者的故事得到喘息，可以这么说。

sentences.en: So I'll just give you a very quick sketch of Catherine Eddowes' life, because, again, because we want to sort of let the victim stories breathe, as it were.
sentences.zh: 我们会在奖励剧集中讲她。

sentences.en: We'll be doing her in the bonus episode.
sentences.zh: 她1842年出生在伍尔弗汉普顿，父母非常年轻，来自马口铁加工背景。

sentences.en: She's born in Wolverhampton in 1842 to very young parents who came from tinplate working backgrounds.
sentences.zh: 他们搬到伦敦，英年早逝。

sentences.en: They move to London, and they die young.
sentences.zh: 她最终成了孤儿。

sentences.en: She ends up as an orphan.
sentences.zh: 她来来回回，去了伯明翰、伍尔弗汉普顿、伦敦，最后和一个叫托马斯·康威的士兵在一起。

sentences.en: She goes sort of back and forth, but to Birmingham, Wolverhampton, London, she ends up with a soldier called Thomas Conway.
sentences.zh: 这就是她的一生。

sentences.en: She lives with him for almost 20 years.
sentences.zh: 她和他在一起生活了近20年。

sentences.en: They have three children.
sentences.zh: 他们有三个孩子。

sentences.en: The classic pattern, she drinks.
sentences.zh: 典型的模式，她酗酒。

sentences.en: He's probably violent.
sentences.zh: 他很可能有暴力倾向。

sentences.en: They separate.
sentences.zh: 他们分开了。

sentences.en: I think he definitely is violent, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 我觉得他绝对有暴力倾向，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because she's always got kind of black eyes and things.
sentences.zh: 因为她总是带着黑眼圈之类的伤痕。

sentences.en: They're into the downward spiral.
sentences.zh: 他们陷入了恶性循环。

sentences.en: She ends up with John Kelly.
sentences.zh: 她最终和约翰·凯利在一起了。

sentences.en: She works as a child woman doing odd jobs, but she's almost certainly involved with casual prostitution as well.
sentences.zh: 她做些零工，但几乎可以肯定她也从事零星的卖淫活动。

sentences.en: So it's unclear.
sentences.zh: 所以情况不明。

sentences.en: They've just been hot picking in Kent, her and this guy, Kelly.
sentences.zh: 她和这个叫凯利的家伙刚在肯特郡采过啤酒花。

sentences.en: Because hot picking is kind of almost the nearest holiday that you have if you're kind of on the streets, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 因为如果你流落街头，采啤酒花几乎是你唯一的度假方式，不是吗？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And tens of thousands of people would go hot picking in Kent and so on.
sentences.zh: 成千上万的人会去肯特郡采啤酒花等等。

sentences.en: They've gone off.
sentences.zh: 他们离开了。

sentences.en: They've come back.
sentences.zh: 他们又回来了。

sentences.en: She's got drunk.
sentences.zh: 她喝醉了。

sentences.en: She's actually picked up earlier on the Saturday for being drunk by the police.
sentences.zh: 事实上，她在周六早些时候因为醉酒被警察带走了。

sentences.en: She's put in a cell.
sentences.zh: 她被关进了牢房。

sentences.en: The police let her out at one o'clock on the Sunday morning.
sentences.zh: 警察在周日凌晨一点把她放了出来。

sentences.en: Her last words, recorded words, to the constable who lets her out.
sentences.zh: 她对放她出来的警员说的最后一句话，也是有记录的话。

sentences.en: She says to him, all right, good night, old cock.
sentences.zh: 她对他说，好吧，晚安，老兄。

sentences.en: And then about 40 minutes later, she is dead.
sentences.zh: 大约40分钟后，她就死了。

sentences.en: So the ripper, you know, struck very quickly after she was let out.
sentences.zh: 所以开膛手在她被释放后很快就下手了。

sentences.en: Now, as I've already heard, her fate is by far the most horrific so far.
sentences.zh: 正如我之前听到的，她的遭遇是目前为止最恐怖的。

sentences.en: Her throat has been cut for seven inches from left to right.
sentences.zh: 她的喉咙被从左到右割开了七英寸。

sentences.en: Her face and body have been horribly mutilated.
sentences.zh: 她的脸和身体受到了极其残忍的毁坏。

sentences.en: Her torso has been ripped open, her insides removed and put by her shoulder.
sentences.zh: 她的躯干被剖开，内脏被取出并放在她的肩旁。

sentences.en: And the killer has left with her left kidney and part of her uterus.
sentences.zh: 凶手带走了她的左肾和部分子宫。

sentences.en: He has also cut off the lobe of one of her ears, hasn't he?
sentences.zh: 他还割下了她的一只耳垂，对吧？

sentences.en: And this kind of resonates because in the notorious letter where Jack the Ripper introduces himself, he'd said that he would cut off the ears of his next victim.
sentences.zh: 这引起了共鸣，因为在杰克开膛手自称的那封臭名昭著的信中，他曾说要割下下一个受害者的耳朵。

sentences.en: And so this debate as to whether cutting off one lobe counts or not.
sentences.zh: 所以关于割下一个耳垂是否算数，存在争议。

sentences.en: That is right.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: What the killer does not do is to cut off her ears, though, which the letter had said that he would.
sentences.zh: 不过，凶手并没有割下她的耳朵，尽管信中曾说他会这么做。

sentences.en: And cutting off the lobe in the context of the general mutilations is only a small thing.
sentences.zh: 在整体毁尸的背景下，割下耳垂只是小事一桩。

sentences.en: It doesn't seem like a deliberate thing that you've done to justify a boast in a letter beforehand.
sentences.zh: 这看起来不像是有意为之，无法证明信中吹嘘的真实性。

sentences.en: Anyway, the surgeon who looked at the body,
sentences.zh: 总之，检查尸体的外科医生，

sentences.en: Dr. Frederick Gordon Brown, was sure that the killer had done this on the spot within moments.
sentences.zh: 弗雷德里克·戈登·布朗医生，确信凶手是在现场瞬间完成的。

sentences.en: So later on, when we get to the mad conspiracy theories, the idea that the victim's bodies were mutilated in a carriage by a royal doctor and then dumped on the spot.
sentences.zh: 所以后来，当我们谈到那些疯狂的阴谋论时，关于受害者尸体是由皇家医生在马车里毁坏然后抛尸现场的说法，

sentences.en: This is not what people thought at the time when they inspected the bodice.
sentences.zh: 这并不是当时检查尸体的人所想的那样。

sentences.en: Dr. Gordon Brown also thought the killer must have had a degree of expertise.
sentences.zh: 戈登·布朗医生还认为凶手一定具备一定的专业知识。

sentences.en: He told the Daily News the left kidney had been carefully taken out in such a manner as to show that it had been done by somebody who not only knew its anatomical position,
sentences.zh: 他告诉《每日新闻》，左肾被小心地取出，这种方式表明凶手不仅知道其解剖位置，

sentences.en: but knew how to remove it.
sentences.zh: 而且知道如何将其取出。

sentences.en: Now, again, does this mean that it's a doctor or a surgeon?
sentences.zh: 那么，这是否意味着凶手是医生或外科医生？

sentences.en: No, not necessarily.
sentences.zh: 不，不一定。

sentences.en: It could be, as we've said, a butcher or a slaughterman or a medical student or indeed a very talented amateur who's studied anatomy.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所说，他可能是屠夫、屠宰工、医学生，或者确实是一个研究过解剖学的非常有天赋的业余爱好者。

sentences.en: Somebody who basically knows what they're doing, I guess.
sentences.zh: 我想，就是一个基本知道自己在做什么的人。

sentences.en: Someone who's used to stalking deer on the highlands, perhaps.
sentences.zh: 也许是一个习惯在高地猎鹿的人。

sentences.en: Maybe.
sentences.zh: 也许吧。

sentences.en: So as with
sentences.zh: 所以和

sentences.en: Elizabeth Stride's murder, there is one interesting witness account.
sentences.zh: 伊丽莎白·斯泰德的谋杀案一样，有一个有趣的目击者证词。

sentences.en: There are two friends, they're both Jewish, a guy called
sentences.zh: 有两位朋友，他们都是犹太人，一个叫

sentences.en: Joseph Lavender, a commercial traveller, and Joseph Levy, a butcher.
sentences.zh: 约瑟夫·拉文德，是一名商业旅行者，还有约瑟夫·利维，是一名屠夫。

sentences.en: And they were leaving a local social club at half past one or thereabouts when they saw a man and woman standing at the entrance to a nearby alley and Lavender saw
sentences.zh: 他们在一点半左右离开当地的一家社交俱乐部时，看到一男一女站在附近一条小巷的入口处，拉文德看到了

sentences.en: the most clearly.
sentences.zh: 最清楚的情况。

sentences.en: Well, he didn't see the woman's face, so he couldn't be sure that it was Catherine Eddowes.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他没看清女人的脸，所以不能确定那是凯瑟琳·埃多斯。

sentences.en: But he said the man was about 30, about 5 foot 7 with a moustache, medium build and a peaked deer stalker's cap.
sentences.zh: 但他描述那个男人大约30岁，身高约5英尺7英寸，留着胡子，中等身材，戴着尖顶猎鹿帽。

sentences.en: But he thought the man looked rough and shabby.
sentences.zh: 但他觉得那个男人看起来粗鲁且衣衫褴褛。

sentences.en: So we've had slightly different accounts of how the man looks, but there are a few common features, aren't there?
sentences.zh: 所以我们对那个男人的外貌有略微不同的描述，但有一些共同特征，不是吗？

sentences.en: There are, and also it's the middle of the night, flickering of the gas lamps.
sentences.zh: 确实，而且当时是深夜，煤气灯忽明忽暗。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And this time there is another clue, a very strange and disturbing clue.
sentences.zh: 这一次还有另一个线索，一个非常奇怪且令人不安的线索。

sentences.en: So within minutes of Catherine Eddowes' murder, the police were scouring this kind of warren of streets around Mitre Square.
sentences.zh: 在凯瑟琳·埃多斯遇害后的几分钟内，警察就在米特广场周围的迷宫般的街道上搜查。

sentences.en: And as we've described, once again, the killer slipped through their fingers like a ghoSt.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所描述的，凶手再次像幽灵一样从他们指缝间溜走了。

sentences.en: Five minutes away, a guy called
sentences.zh: 五分钟路程外，一个叫

sentences.en: Alfred Long, police constable, is patrolling
sentences.zh: 阿尔弗雷德·朗的警员正在巡逻

sentences.en: Galston Street, which is on the sort of boundary between the city and Whitechapel.
sentences.zh: 加尔斯顿街，这条街位于伦敦城和白教堂区的边界上。

sentences.en: And at 2.55, he spotted something in a tenement doorway and it was a woman's apron wet with blood.
sentences.zh: 凌晨2点55分，他在一个公寓门口发现了一些东西，那是一条沾满血迹的女性围裙。

sentences.en: And it turns out that this is
sentences.zh: 结果发现这就是

sentences.en: Catherine Eddowes' apron.
sentences.zh: 凯瑟琳·埃多斯的围裙。

sentences.en: And he looks around for other signs of blood or any of the other clues, and then he sees something else.
sentences.zh: 他环顾四周寻找其他血迹或任何其他线索，然后他看到了别的东西。

sentences.en: To the right of the doorway, written in white chalk on the black bricks, are the words, the Jews are the men that will not be blamed for nothing.
sentences.zh: 在门口右侧，黑砖墙上用白粉笔写着一行字：犹太人是不会因任何事而受到指责的人。

sentences.en: And the word
sentences.zh: 而单词

sentences.en: Jews is spelt
sentences.zh: 犹太人（Jews）拼写为

sentences.en: J-U-W-E-S.
sentences.zh: J-U-W-E-S。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So PC Long takes the apron to the nearest police station.
sentences.zh: 于是朗警员把围裙带到了最近的警察局。

sentences.en: Soon, lots of other policemen are swarming around these buildings.
sentences.zh: 很快，许多其他警察蜂拥到这些建筑物周围。

sentences.en: They don't find anything.
sentences.zh: 他们什么也没发现。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, the police superintendent,
sentences.zh: 与此同时，警察局长

sentences.en: Thomas Arnold, briefs the Met Commissioner,
sentences.zh: 托马斯·阿诺德向伦敦警察厅厅长

sentences.en: Sir Charles Warren, about this graffiti.
sentences.zh: 查尔斯·沃伦爵士汇报了这些涂鸦。

sentences.en: And the superintendent says,
sentences.zh: 局长说，

sentences.en: I want to get rid of this as quickly as possible.
sentences.zh: 我想尽快处理掉它。

sentences.en: If we leave it up on the wall, by dawn there will be a riot against the Jews of the East End.
sentences.zh: 如果我们把它留在墙上，到黎明时分，东区的犹太人就会发生暴乱。

sentences.en: And you can completely see why he says this.
sentences.zh: 你完全可以理解他为什么这么说。

sentences.en: Passions are running high because of the tide of immigration in the 1880s.
sentences.zh: 由于19世纪80年代的移民潮，人们情绪高涨。

sentences.en: And as we saw after Annie Chapman's murder, there are a lot of people who are very keen to blame the Jews of the East End.
sentences.zh: 正如我们在安妮·查普曼遇害后看到的那样，有很多人非常热衷于指责东区的犹太人。

sentences.en: Sir Charles Warren goes personally to Galston Street and he looks at the writing and the graffiti.
sentences.zh: 查尔斯·沃伦爵士亲自前往加尔斯顿街，查看了那段文字和涂鸦。

sentences.en: Some of the people say, should we wait for a photographer to photograph the graffiti?
sentences.zh: 有人说，我们要不要等摄影师来给涂鸦拍照？

sentences.en: And he says, no, it's getting light.
sentences.zh: 他说，不，天快亮了。

sentences.en: We cannot risk people seeing it.
sentences.zh: 我们不能冒着被人看到的风险。

sentences.en: And so at 5.30, as dawn is breaking, the chalk is wiped away.
sentences.zh: 于是凌晨5点30分，天刚破晓，粉笔字就被擦掉了。

sentences.en: And so, you know, we have no photo of it.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我们没有它的照片。

sentences.en: So the enduring mystery, who left it?
sentences.zh: 那么，持久的谜团是，是谁留下的？

sentences.en: What does it mean?
sentences.zh: 它意味着什么？

sentences.en: There are three possibilities.
sentences.zh: 有三种可能性。

sentences.en: Number one, it's a complete coincidence.
sentences.zh: 第一，这完全是个巧合。

sentences.en: The ripper just threw the apron away and there was some anti-Semitic graffiti on the wall.
sentences.zh: 开膛手只是扔掉了围裙，而墙上恰好有一些反犹太涂鸦。

sentences.en: The police themselves didn't agree whether some people said it was fresh, some people said it was faded.
sentences.zh: 警察自己也没达成一致，有人说它是新的，有人说它是褪色的。

sentences.en: So it could be old anti-Semitic graffiti.
sentences.zh: 所以这可能是旧的反犹太涂鸦。

sentences.en: Of course, there is a fair bit of anti-Semitic graffiti in the East End.
sentences.zh: 当然，东区确实有不少反犹太涂鸦。

sentences.en: However,
sentences.zh: 然而，

sentences.en: Philip Sugden points out, this was a building that had a lot of Jewish residents.
sentences.zh: 菲利普·萨格登指出，这是一栋有很多犹太居民的建筑。

sentences.en: Is it really plausible that they wouldn't have wiped it away?
sentences.zh: 他们没把它擦掉真的合理吗？

sentences.en: I mean, if it had been someone who'd put it up half an hour before, perfectly plausible.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果是半小时前刚写上去的，那完全合理。

sentences.en: I suppose, Tom, but that really is a coincidence, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我想这确实是个巧合，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, it is a coincidence, but I assume that this kind of graffiti is going up all the time.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个巧合，但我认为这种涂鸦一直都在出现。

sentences.en: In the middle of the night?
sentences.zh: 在半夜？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well,
sentences.zh: 嗯，

sentences.en: I'm not sure.
sentences.zh: 我不确定。

sentences.en: That seems to me, I have to say, the likeliest explanation.
sentences.zh: 我必须说，这对我来说似乎是最可能的解释。

sentences.en: Explanation two,
sentences.zh: 解释二，

sentences.en: listeners can make up their own minds, Tom.
sentences.zh: 听众可以自己做决定，汤姆。

sentences.en: We don't want to preach.
sentences.zh: 我们不想说教。

sentences.en: That's the last thing we do on the rest of this history.
sentences.zh: 那是我们在本历史节目中最后会做的事。

sentences.en: Just offering my own conclusions.
sentences.zh: 只是提供我自己的结论。

sentences.en: Well, everyone's grateful for that and everyone enjoys it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，大家都对此心存感激，也都乐在其中。

sentences.en: No one more than me, to be honeSt.
sentences.zh: 老实说，没人比我更享受了。

sentences.en: So the next thing, the Ripper left the message to taunt the police because he was Jewish.
sentences.zh: 所以第二种可能，开膛手留下这条信息是为了嘲弄警察，因为他是犹太人。

sentences.en: So he's euphoric from his killings.
sentences.zh: 所以他因杀戮而感到狂喜。

sentences.en: He's in a state of ecstasy.
sentences.zh: 他处于一种极度兴奋的状态。

sentences.en: He's putting two fingers up to the world and saying, ha ha, the Jews have got their own back.
sentences.zh: 他向世界竖起中指，仿佛在说，哈哈，犹太人已经报复了。
